subject: biology
title: Producing monoclonal antibodies
key_idea: Monoclonal antibodies are identical antibodies that are all specific to one antigen. They are made by fusing a lymphocyte with a tumour cell to form a hybridoma. The hybridoma is cloned, and the cells make large amounts of the antibody.

blocks.text: This topic is for separate biology. Antibodies are made by lymphocytes, but a lymphocyte cannot divide many times in the laboratory. Scientists solve this by combining it with a tumour cell.

items.meaning: An antibody made by a clone of identical cells, so every antibody is specific to the same antigen.
A white blood cell that makes antibodies.
A cancer cell that divides rapidly.
A cell made by combining a lymphocyte with a tumour cell. It makes the antibody and divides rapidly.

items: Monoclonal antibodies are all identical and specific to one antigen.
A hybridoma has the antibody-making ability of a lymphocyte and the rapid division of a tumour cell.

blocks.text: Monoclonal antibodies are usually made using mouse lymphocytes. The steps are in a fixed order.

diagram.alt: Put the stages of producing monoclonal antibodies in order, from injecting the antigen into a mouse to collecting the antibody.
diagram.prompt: Put the stages of making monoclonal antibodies in the correct order.
steps: The antigen (protein) is injected into a mouse
Lymphocytes that make the specific antibody are collected from the mouse
The lymphocytes are combined with tumour cells to make hybridoma cells
A hybridoma that makes the correct (specific) antibody is found
The hybridoma is cloned to produce many identical cells
The antibody is collected and purified

items: The antigen is injected into a mouse. The mouse lymphocytes make antibodies against it.
Lymphocytes that make the specific antibody are collected.
These are fused with tumour cells to make **hybridoma** cells.
The hybridoma that makes the correct antibody is isolated.
It is **cloned**, so many identical cells are produced and all make the same antibody.
The antibody is collected and purified.
Lymphocytes from an injected mouse are combined with tumour cells to make hybridomas.
The correct hybridoma is cloned, giving many cells that all make the same antibody.

blocks.text: Mice are not the only source. Some people prefer methods that do not use animals.

items: Human lymphocytes made naturally after an infection can be used instead of mouse lymphocytes.
Genes for many different antibodies are put into viruses. When an antigen attaches to one, its gene is used to genetically engineer bacteria, which make large quantities of that antibody.
These methods do not use mice. Some people think using mice is cruel or unethical.
Using bacteria and viruses means mice are not needed.
People may object to the original method because it uses animals.

checks.q: Name the cell made when a lymphocyte is combined with a tumour cell.
Explain why a tumour cell is used to make monoclonal antibodies.
checks.a: The tumour cell divides rapidly, so the hybridoma can be cloned to make many cells that all produce the antibody.

checks.q: Describe what is done to a hybridoma cell to produce large amounts of antibody.
checks.a: It is cloned to produce many identical cells. All the cells make the same antibody, which is collected and purified.

exam_phrases: extract / collect (mouse) lymphocytes that make a specific antibody
lymphocytes are combined with a tumour cell to create a hybridoma
(hybridoma) cloned to create many cells that produce the antibody
all the cells make the same antibody

mistakes.wrong: White blood cells are combined with tumour cells.
mistakes.right: "White blood cells" is ignored here. Say lymphocytes (T or B lymphocytes) are combined with tumour or cancer cells to make hybridoma cells.

mistakes.wrong: The stem cells are cloned to make the antibodies.
mistakes.right: Cloning the original stem cells is not credited. It is the hybridoma that is cloned.
"Tumour" unqualified is ignored. Say the lymphocyte is combined with a tumour cell to make a hybridoma.

worked_example.question:
Scientists have produced monoclonal antibodies for HIV. The monoclonal antibodies can prevent a person infected with HIV developing AIDS.

Describe how the monoclonal antibody for HIV can be produced.
answer_points: HIV (an antigen or protein from it) is injected into a mouse.
Lymphocytes that make a specific antibody to HIV are extracted or collected.
The lymphocytes are combined with a tumour cell to create a hybridoma.
The hybridoma is cloned to create many cells that produce the antibody.
worked_example.tip: Another route also scores: the hybridoma that makes the correct antibody is isolated, and then cloned.

exam_phrases: lymphocytes fused with tumour cells to make hybridoma cells

mistakes.wrong: Monoclonal antibodies are made by lymphocytes alone.
mistakes.right: A lymphocyte is fused with a tumour cell to make a hybridoma cell. It divides rapidly, so the antibody can be made in large amounts.

exam_phrases: hybridoma make antibodies against the drug

mistakes.wrong: People prefer the bacteria method because of religion.
mistakes.right: References to religion or "playing god" are ignored. Say the method does not use mice or animals, which some people think is cruel or unethical.

worked_example.question:
Methamphetamine is a drug. Scientists are investigating the use of antibodies as a treatment to control the negative effects of the drug.

As the human body does not naturally make antibodies against methamphetamine, scientists are using mice to make antibodies.

Describe how large amounts of the antibodies can be made using monoclonal antibody techniques.
answer_points: The lymphocytes are fused with tumour cells.
The hybridoma cells make antibodies against methamphetamine (the drug).
worked_example.tip: Any four of these points score one mark each.
